questions.question:
Select the correct Passive Voice form of the given sentence:
'The computer assistant updates the judicial software every month.'

options.text: The judicial software is updated by the computer assistant every month.
The judicial software was updated by the computer assistant every month.
The judicial software is being updated by the computer assistant every month.
The judicial software has been updated by the computer assistant every month.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Present ('updates') mein hai. Naya subject 'The judicial software' singular noun hai. Simple Present passive formula: 'is + V3' ➔ 'is updated' (A). Option (B) Simple Past mein tense distort karta hai. Option (C) continuous aspect jodta hai aur (D) perfect tense jodta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Simple Present Passive = Object + is / am / are + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform the following sentence into Passive Voice:
'The technical team is configuring the biometric attendance machines.'

options.text: The biometric attendance machines are configured by the technical team.
The biometric attendance machines are being configured by the technical team.
The biometric attendance machines were being configured by the technical team.
The biometric attendance machines have been configured by the technical team.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Continuous ('is configuring') mein hai. Naya subject 'The biometric attendance machines' plural noun hai, isliye plural auxiliary 'are' + continuous marker 'being' + V3 'configured' ➔ 'are being configured' (B) sahi hai. Option (A) mein 'being' omit hai jisse wo Simple Present ban gaya. Option (C) Past tense hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Present Continuous Passive = Object + is/am/are + being + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The administrative officer has notified the revised promotion rosters.'

options.text: The revised promotion rosters has been notified by the administrative officer.
The revised promotion rosters have been notified by the administrative officer.
The revised promotion rosters were notified by the administrative officer.
The revised promotion rosters had been notified by the administrative officer.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Perfect ('has notified') mein hai. Active subject singular ('officer') tha, lekin naya subject 'The revised promotion rosters' plural noun hai. Isliye passive auxiliary naye subject ke hisaab se plural 'have been' banegi: 'The revised promotion rosters have been notified...' (B). Option (A) plural subject ke sath singular 'has' laga kar agreement error karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Passive auxiliary concord naye subject ke number aur person par depend karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Select the correct Passive Voice conversion:
'The sessions judge granted conditional bail to the accused yesterday.'

options.text: Conditional bail was granted to the accused by the sessions judge yesterday.
Conditional bail had been granted to the accused by the sessions judge yesterday.
Conditional bail is granted to the accused by the sessions judge yesterday.
Conditional bail was being granted to the accused by the sessions judge yesterday.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'granted' Simple Past (V2) tense mein hai. Naya subject 'Conditional bail' singular uncountable noun hai. Simple Past passive formula: 'was + V3' ➔ 'was granted' (A). Option (B) Past Perfect ('had been granted') banata hai jo tense backshift error hai. Option (C) Present tense hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Simple Past Passive = Object + was / were + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The investigating team did not find any incriminating documents.'

options.text: Any incriminating documents were not found by the investigating team.
No incriminating documents were found by the investigating team.
Incriminating documents did not found by the investigating team.
No incriminating documents was found by the investigating team.

questions.explanation: Standard formal English syntax mein active 'did not find any' passive mein subject position par aate waqt 'No + Plural Noun + were + V3' ban jata hai: 'No incriminating documents were found by the investigating team.' (B). 'Any... not found' (A) awkward aur non-idiomatic lagta hai. Option (C) mein 'did' copy kar diya gaya hai. Option (D) mein plural 'documents' ke sath singular 'was' laga hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04 & Section E: Not any + Object (active) ➔ No + Object + were + V3 (passive).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The full court committee was discussing the recruitment vacancies.'

options.text: The recruitment vacancies was being discussed by the full court committee.
The recruitment vacancies were discussed by the full court committee.
The recruitment vacancies were being discussed by the full court committee.
The recruitment vacancies had been discussed by the full court committee.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'was discussing' Past Continuous hai aur naya subject 'The recruitment vacancies' plural noun hai. Isliye plural auxiliary 'were' + continuous marker 'being' + V3 'discussed' ➔ 'were being discussed' (C) correct hai. Option (A) mein singular 'was' hai, Option (B) mein 'being' omit hai, aur Option (D) Past Perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Past Continuous Passive = Plural Object + were + being + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The administrative registrar had locked the treasury vault before sunset.'

options.text: The treasury vault was locked by the administrative registrar before sunset.
The treasury vault had been locked by the administrative registrar before sunset.
The treasury vault has been locked by the administrative registrar before sunset.
The treasury vault had locked by the administrative registrar before sunset.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Past Perfect ('had locked') mein hai. Past Perfect passive ka universal formula hai: 'had + been + V3'. Isliye 'had been locked' (B) sahi hai. Option (A) Simple Past hai, Option (C) Present Perfect hai, aur Option (D) mein 'been' gayab hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Past Perfect Passive = Object + had + been + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Select the correct Passive Voice conversion:
'The recruitment board will declare the final merit cutoffs on Friday.'

options.text: The final merit cutoffs will be declared by the recruitment board on Friday.
The final merit cutoffs will declared by the recruitment board on Friday.
The final merit cutoffs would be declared by the recruitment board on Friday.
The final merit cutoffs will have been declared by the recruitment board on Friday.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'will declare' Simple Future tense mein hai. Simple Future passive formula: 'will/shall + be + V3' ➔ 'will be declared' (A). Option (B) mein 'be' omit hai. Option (C) mein 'will' ko 'would' mein backshift kiya gaya hai jo Voice mein galat hai. Option (D) Future Perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Simple Future Passive = will / shall + be + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The system administrator will have completed the network audit by 5 PM.'

options.text: The network audit will be completed by the system administrator by 5 PM.
The network audit will have been completed by the system administrator by 5 PM.
The network audit will has been completed by the system administrator by 5 PM.
The network audit would have been completed by the system administrator by 5 PM.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'will have completed' Future Perfect tense mein hai. Future Perfect passive formula: 'will have been + V3' ➔ 'will have been completed' (B). Option (A) Simple Future hai. Option (C) modal ke baad 'has' lagata hai jo ungrammatical hai. Option (D) conditional would use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Future Perfect Passive = will / shall + have + been + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Did the judicial magistrate issue the search warrant?'

options.text: Did the search warrant issued by the judicial magistrate?
Was the search warrant issued by the judicial magistrate?
Had the search warrant been issued by the judicial magistrate?
Is the search warrant issued by the judicial magistrate?

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past Yes/No question ('Did + Subject + V1?') hai. Passive banate waqt 'Did' hat jata hai aur naye singular subject 'the search warrant' ke mutabiq Simple Past auxiliary 'Was' shuruat mein aati hai: 'Was the search warrant issued by the judicial magistrate?' (B). Option (A) 'Did' retain karta hai, aur Option (C) tense had kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Simple Past Yes/No Interrogative = Was / Were + Object + V3 + (by + Subject)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Who broke the confidential seal of the electronic voting machine?'

options.text: By whom the confidential seal of the electronic voting machine was broken?
By whom was the confidential seal of the electronic voting machine broken?
Who was the confidential seal of the electronic voting machine broken?
By whom had the confidential seal of the electronic voting machine been broken?

questions.explanation: Active 'Who' passive mein 'By whom' ban jata hai. 'By whom' ke turant baad auxiliary verb ka inversion aana zaroori hai: 'By whom + was + Object + V3?'. Isliye (B) correct hai. Option (A) mein inversion missing hai ('seal was broken'). Option (D) mein tense had kar diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Who + V2 + O?' ➔ 'By whom + was/were + O + V3?'. Inversion mandatory hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Why did the administration transfer the senior protocol officer?'

options.text: Why the senior protocol officer was transferred by the administration?
Why was the senior protocol officer transferred by the administration?
Why had the senior protocol officer been transferred by the administration?
Why is the senior protocol officer transferred by the administration?

questions.explanation: Wh-questions mein auxiliary verb hamesha subject se pehle aani chahiye (interrogative word order). Yahan 'Why' ke turant baad auxiliary 'was' aayegi, fir naya subject 'the senior protocol officer', aur fir V3 'transferred': 'Why was the senior protocol officer transferred by the administration?' (B). Option (A) mein assertive word order use kiya gaya hai jo direct question mein fatal error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Wh-word + auxiliary + Object + V3 + (by + Subject)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.subtopic: Agent Omission with Negative Indefinite Pronoun
questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Nobody has claimed the abandoned judicial file from the registry.'

options.text: The abandoned judicial file has been claimed by nobody from the registry.
The abandoned judicial file has not been claimed from the registry.
The abandoned judicial file was not claimed by nobody from the registry.
The abandoned judicial file has not claimed from the registry.

questions.explanation: Active sentence mein subject negative indefinite pronoun 'Nobody' hai. Passive banate waqt sentence negative auxiliary 'has not been claimed' leta hai aur agent 'by nobody' naturally omit ho jata hai: 'The abandoned judicial file has not been claimed from the registry.' (B). Option (A) 'by nobody' lagata hai jo clumsy aur unidiomatic hai. Option (C) double negative ('not... nobody') banata hai. Option (D) mein 'been' omit hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Section G: Subject 'Nobody + affirmative verb' passive mein 'Negative auxiliary (not been V3)' ban jata hai aur agent omit ho jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
What is the Passive Voice of:
'The key prosecution witness collapsed in the court corridor this afternoon.'?

options.text: The court corridor was collapsed by the key prosecution witness this afternoon.
The key prosecution witness was collapsed in the court corridor this afternoon.
No Passive Voice transformation is possible.
The court corridor had been collapsed in by the witness this afternoon.

questions.explanation: Verb 'collapsed' is context mein strictly intransitive verb hai. 'Collapsed' ke baad 'in the court corridor' place adverbial prepositional phrase hai, direct object nahi. Chunki sentence mein koi direct object nahi hai, isliye iska koi passive transformation possible nahi hai. Option (B) 'was collapsed' kehna pseudo-passive blunder hai. Option (A) 'court corridor was collapsed' absurd meaning banata hai. Correct answer (C) 'No Passive Voice transformation is possible' hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Section H: Purely intransitive verbs without a direct object cannot form passive voice.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting in Passive Voice Construction
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
'(A) All the defective writ petitions / (B) were returned to the registry / (C) because the essential annexures / (D) were not being attached properly.'

options.text: (A) All the defective writ petitions
(B) were returned to the registry
(C) because the essential annexures
(D) were not being attached properly

questions.explanation: Part (D) mein error hai. Context completed state/result ko express kar raha hai ('petitions were returned because annexures had not been attached'). Completed unfulfilled requirement ke liye Past Perfect passive 'had not been attached' lagna chahiye, ongoing 'were not being attached' nahi. Annexures attach hone ka kaam petition return hone se pehle ka tha, isliye aspectual discord hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & Section I: Prior completed conditions demand Past Perfect Passive ('had not been attached').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04
